March, 2023 the students of 4

Semester, MBA got the opportunity to attend a guest lecture by Dr. Gopal Babu of Value Education Cell (AKGEC) on the topic “Sambandho Mein Bhaav Ka Mahatav”. The session started with a simple breathing exercise which helped the students to feel more relaxed.

The light was thrown on the importance of connection i.e having a connection with others that is based on feelings and not on the basis of our thoughts. Communication is the vital key to forming connections with those around us. Observation and Conclusion are the key points in understanding the person we are trying to communicate with. In order to show how these two work, we were shown a short role play where the students enacted out roles, and the rest of the students had to figure out and tell whether the characters were communication on the basis of observation or conclusion.

Often, we form opinions/conclusions about others that are irrational on the basis of our past experiences. It is necessary for us to view the situation in the perspective of the present time. Thus, our feelings and how we act upon them are to be taken into consideration as they define our relations with others in the long run.

It was an insightful and a marvelous session, the students enjoyed it thoroughly and we look forward to have many more informative sessions. It was an honour to have Dr. Gopal Babu with us and we are grateful to him for enlightening us with his knowledge.

The 5-Day UHV-II Refresher Workshop, approved by the All-India Council for Technical Education (AICTE), commenced from 28th July- 1st August 2025 at Ajay Kumar Garg Engineering College, Ghaziabad. This workshop serves both as a refresher for the Universal Human Values (UHV-II) Workshop and a preparatory platform for the upcoming UHV-III Workshop.

A total of 37 participants registered from the host institution and various external colleges, and 31 participants attended actively. The attendees primarily comprise faculty members who have previously undergone the UHV-I and UHV-II workshops and are now engaging in a deeper exploration of human values in education.
Workshop Objectives and Approach

A total of five sessions, including one small group discussion (GD) session, helped participants to explore and express themselves thoroughly. The whole workshop is designed to deepen participants’ understanding of human values through experiential learning, reflective dialogue, and participative exploration. It reinforces key concepts from UHV-II and lays a robust foundation for advanced learning in UHV-III.
The opening sessions guided participants to reflect on fundamental human aspirations: • Do we want to live? • Do we want to live with fulfilment? • Or do we want to live with continuous fulfilment?

Participants explored the meaning of continuous fulfilment based on natural acceptance, gradually transitioning toward observing their own internal state, rather than forming premature conclusions. The first step in this self-inquiry—observing the state of imagination and identifying the source of desire—was received with appreciation and enthusiasm.

Exploration of Happiness and Harmony A key theme explored during the workshop was happiness as harmony at all levels of human existence: • At the Individual level: Harmony between the self (conscious unit) and the body (material unit) • In the Family: Nine essential feelings for harmony, from trust to love, are seen as coexisting naturally • In Society: Four comprehensive goals (right understanding, prosperity, trust, and mutual fulfilment) are identified as coexisting harmoniously • In Nature/Existence: Four distinct orders of nature (material, plant, animal, and human) are understood to be in mutually fulfilling coexistence • In the larger Existence: All units of nature are in coexistence with the all-pervading space

This understanding reinforces that coexistence as the absolute truth is reflected at every level of human living. Recognizing this truth fosters a holistic and values-based worldview that integrates thought, behaviour, and interaction with the world.

Their continued guidance plays a pivotal role in enabling educators to integrate Universal Human Values into the educational framework meaningfully. blocks.text: The following were the highlights of the workshop-
It was an unstructured workshop, where the experiential learning was in the Centre.
The workshop was specifically focused on observing feelings/emotions of the immediate moment (being aware and honest about – Here and Now).

Time, Territory and Task were cautiously cared for, disallowing any past reference or future assumptions ie avoiding Then or There), while interacting and dealing with participants and self-planned tasks.
The present was emphasized as the best-owned reality one can see.
Self-Image was recognized as a big challenge rather main culprit, responsible for the unawareness about feelings and behavioural ambiguities.
Availability of feelings, and acknowledging them, facilitates natural expression in behaviour. The same was exercised.
Expression has a CHOICE, may be verbal/nonverbal/pictorial/violent/nonviolent. The same was discussed and experienced.
The following were the main observations in the workshop-
The process connects with the first step of EXERCISE 1 of UHV, ie seeing the Self by the Self (without any reaction or evaluation).
Every moment of awareness about our being was been practiced formally.
The process is complementary to developing competence in observing feelings (emotions).
The existence (goal) is one similar reality, but the process/mechanism to know/understand the existence is variable.
Extracted Recommendations after the workshop were-
Integration of efficient steps (from various processes) may be evolved to suit the human desire of KNOWING/ UNDERSTANDING.
Participant’s periodic follow-up (online) is desirable to evaluate the gradual transformation.

Frequent such short crisp workshops may be planned, purposely for experiential validation (Steps of Exercise 1 and 2), for intense UHV explorers. This idea was shared with the honorable DG for his kind consideration.

Workshop on “Conscious Engineering”
Executive Summary:
Dates: 30 August – 6 September 2025 Venue: ME Conference Hall, ME Block, AKGEC Total Registrations: 57 Participants Reported: 51 Successful Completions: 35

The Value Education (VE) Cell at Ajay Kumar Garg Engineering College organized a transformative 36-hour student workshop titled “Consciousness Engineering” from 30 August to 6 September 2025. The sessions were led by esteemed facilitators Dr. Gopal Babu and Dr. Manishi Mishra , with coordination support from Aman Singh, Sai Nainsi Keshari, and the VE Cell team.

This workshop offered students a structured opportunity to explore the science of self-awareness, emotional intelligence, and conscious living. Participants engaged in introspective practices to observe their thoughts, feelings, and deep-rooted conditioning (sanskaras), fostering a deeper understanding of human behavior and relationships.

Objectives The workshop was designed to achieve the following developmental goals: • Cultivate self-awareness and emotional sensitivity • Enhance self-counseling and introspection skills • Improve interpersonal understanding and empathy • Strengthen emotional regulation and response management • Foster collaborative and team-oriented behavior • Promote mindful listening and communication • Encourage ethical discernment and value-based decision-making
Participants and Faculty Involvement • Total Registrations: 57 students • Reported Attendance: 51 students • Successful Completions: 35 students
Additionally, 6 students from RKGIM College participated, accompanied by Dr. Arun Kumar Pandey, whose presence enriched the diversity and depth of discussions.
Faculty members Dr. Upasana and Dr. Parul actively engaged in daily sessions, contributing to the learning environment. The workshop was conducted under the overall guidance of Mr. B. N. Pandey .
Workshop Structure and Daily Themes

The workshop was divided into eight sessions over eight days, blending weekday evening sessions with full-day weekend engagements. Each day focused on a distinct theme, supported by interactive activities, meditation, and reflection.

Student Reflections and Impact During the final sharing session, students expressed meaningful personal transformations: • Improved focus and reduced distractions • Enhanced ability to observe thoughts and regulate emotions • Strengthened relationships with peers and family • Shifted perspective from judging competence to trusting intention • Greater appreciation for natural human values

Commitments and Future Engagements Participants pledged to: • Encourage peers and family to attend future workshops • Actively support VE Cell initiatives • Volunteer for social programs such as Kartavya (tree adoption), teaching in government schools, and sustainability efforts

Conclusion and Closing Remarks The Consciousness Engineering Workshop successfully empowered students with tools for introspection, emotional clarity, and value-based living. Through experiential learning and guided reflection, participants gained insights into the nine foundational human feelings: Trust, Respect, Affection, Care, Guidance, Reverence, Glory, Gratitude, and Love.

The workshop concluded with a heartfelt Vote of Thanks by Sparsh Trivedi, followed by a group photograph session to commemorate the journey. The final session ended at 06:08 PM, leaving behind a legacy of conscious growth and community spirit.

Workshop on “Understanding Science of Relationships through Self-Exploration” (13-17 Jan, 2025)
Workshop on “Understanding Science of Relationships through Self-Exploration”

Dates: 13-17 January 2025 Duration: 10-hour student workshop divided in 5 days (On weekdays, from 4:30-6:30pm Place: Mini Seminar Hall-1, 2 Total Registrations – 67 Total Participants completed successfully – 53

VE Cell, AKGEC conducted 10 hours of student offline workshop on “Understanding Science of Relationships through Self-Exploration” from 13-17 January 2025. Dr. Upasana Mishra and Dr. Jitendra Chhabra facilitated the workshop. The workshop was conducted as per the following schedule:

a) 13 January 2025 (Monday) – 4:30 PM – 6:30 PM b) 14 January 2025 (Tuesday) – 4:30 PM – 6:30 PM c) 15 January 2025 (Wednesday) – 4:30 PM – 6:30 PM d) 16 January 2025 (Thursday) – 4:30 PM – 6:30 PM e) 17 January 2025 (Friday) – 4:30 PM – 6:30 PM

The objective of the workshop was to help students recognize their innate potential to live a stable and fulfilling life. Instead of providing ready-made solutions, the facilitators encouraged students to explore their daily life challenges, helping them understand the root causes of their problems and discover their own solutions. The workshop was designed as an intense exploration process to guide students towards a better understanding of themselves and their relationships.

The first day of the workshop began with an introduction to the topic and an outline of key checkpoints to be maintained throughout the sessions. The facilitator introduced students to the basic concepts of consciousness and relationships, explaining how the human consciousness often functions logically but lacks in feeling when not aligned with the right understanding. The session emphasized that recognizing one’s inherent potential and right feelings leads to a harmonious and fulfilling life. The facilitators helped students break free from preconceived notions that often lead to unhappiness. Another significant discussion revolved around expectations from others and how with the feeling can lead to a more peaceful life.

From the second day onwards, the facilitator introduced students to nine fundamental feelings, starting with Trust (the foundation value) and ending with Love (the complete value). On the second day, the focus was on Trust, where the facilitator explained the difference between trust and blind trust, helping students understand how trust is ensured in relationships. The discussion then moved to Respect, where a detailed explanation of types of evaluation was provided, helping students to understand how we perceive and respect others.

On the third day, the facilitator elaborated on trust in terms of intention and competence, explaining the difference between trust in intention and evaluation of competence. This helped students understand that people's intentions are right based on natural acceptance even if they lack the competence to execute them effectively. Another key discussion was the difference between Knowledge and Information, emphasizing that knowledge comes from self-exploration, while mere information does not necessarily lead to wisdom. The session also covered the feelings of guidance and affection, showing how they contribute to building strong and meaningful relationships.

The fourth day focused on the next set of values: Care, Guidance, and Reverence. The facilitator explained the importance of genuinely caring for others and their well-being, the role of proper guidance in personal and professional growth, and how reverence develops acceptance for excellence for others based on their living based on right understanding. Students were encouraged to observe their surroundings and reflect on their own experiences. Their queries were resolved through self-exploration, allowing them to understand realities instead of relying solely on external influences.

The final session on the last day of the workshop focused on Love, which was presented as the ultimate or complete value. Love was described as the culmination of all previous values, helping individuals achieve harmony within themselves and with others. The workshop concluded on a highly positive note, with students expressing their gratitude and appreciation for the insights gained. The feedback collected from students indicated high satisfaction, with most of them giving the workshop top ratings for its impact on their understanding of life, relationships, and self-exploration.

This workshop provided students with a unique opportunity to reflect on their inner potential and align their thoughts and actions with values that lead to a harmonious life. Instead of prescribing solutions, the facilitators helped students explore their own answers, making the learning experience deeply personal and transformative.

The workshop’s objective was to help students to see their innate potential to live a happy life. The problem today is that we fail to understand relationship and feelings (values), and consequently we fail to fulfil it despite all our good intentions. The problems are due to the absence of one or more of the right feelings (values) in the Self. And we try to make up this gap by physical facility or by trying to demand these feelings from others, rather than ensuring these feelings in ourselves and sharing it with others. The workshop was based on an intense exploration of these feelings ‘within’, where students validated the proposals in their daily life issues. Utilize their skills with holistic wisdom

Student Induction Program (SIP) (25 Aug-03 Sep, 2025)
Duration: 25 August – 3 September 2025 Prepared in Accordance with: AICTE Guidelines on UHV -I Module Total Duration: 8 Days | 16 Hours Venue: Assigned Lecture Theatres Coordinator – Dr. Parul Verma

Context & Purpose The Universal Human Values (UHV) sessions were a core component of the Student Induction Program (SIP), as mandated by the All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE). These sessions aimed to help students reflect on their basic aspiration and its fulfillment, thereby fostering a holistic understanding of life and education.

Faculty Preparation All assigned faculty members were well-qualified to conduct Universal Human Values (UHV) sessions, having successfully completed the UHV-II workshop as recommended by AICTE. Additionally, senior members of the Value Education Cell organized refresher sessions prior to the Student Induction Program, where key content and anticipated questions were thoroughly reviewed to ensure effective facilitation and preparedness.

Faculty Engagement Faculty Members Assigned: 20 faculty members were assigned to take sessions in 20 sections of B.Tech first students of all branches. 14 faculty members were designated as reserve facilitators, ready to step in and support sessions as needed to ensure smooth execution.
This strategic allocation ensured uninterrupted delivery and allowed flexibility in managing unforeseen challenges.

Program Structure • Total Duration: 16 hours spread across 8 days • Session Format: Interactive lectures, reflective exercises, and feedback sharing • Core Theme: Universal Human Values – understanding basic aspirations of human being and program to ensure its fulfilment leading to holistic development.
Each day was thoughtfully curated to build upon the previous sessions, allowing students to gradually explore and internalize the concepts.

Student Response & Feedback The feedback collected through structured forms and verbal interactions revealed a highly positive reception: • Students expressed deep appreciation for the content and delivery. • Many reported a transformative shift in their perspectives regarding personal growth, relationships, and societal responsibilities. • The proposals of Universal Human Values were not only understood but valued as essential for leading a fulfilling life. • The program was seen as a catalyst for holistic development, aligning academic pursuits with ethical and emotional intelligence.
The induction program successfully laid the foundation for a nurturing and value-based academic environment.

Recommendations for Future Programs • Extend session hours for deeper engagement • Include alumni interactions to share real-life applications of UHV • Introduce creative workshops to complement theoretical discussions • Continue faculty training to maintain high-quality delivery

Conclusion The Universal Human Values sessions during the Student Induction Program were conducted in full alignment with AICTE guidelines and proved to be transformative for the first-year B.Tech students. The sessions laid a strong foundation for value-based education, contributing significantly to the students’ holistic development and well-being.

The College has recognized that UHV (Universal Human Values) concepts are transformative in nature and require time for individuals to fully explore and assimilate. In order to create a conducive environment where students, faculty members, and staff can engage with these concepts, the College has implemented several policies. One of these policies is that each department will hold a UHV seminar every month, led by a faculty member.

The UHV seminars offer an opportunity for participants to engage in deep reflection and dialogue, with the aim of cultivating values such as love, truth and compassion. By exploring UHV concepts, participants will gain a better understanding of themselves, others, and the world around them. Through these seminars, the College aims to foster a community that is committed to personal and collective growth, and to creating positive change in society.

blocks.text: A Spiritual talk by Brahma Kumari (BK) Sangeeta Didi (10 September 2025)
Report on “Why Me?” – Episode 2 Organized by: Value Education Cell, Ajay Kumar Garg Engineering College Date: 10 September 2025 Venue: Main Seminar Hall

The Value Education Cell of Ajay Kumar Garg Engineering College conducted the second episode of its spiritual and introspective series titled “Why Me?”, aimed at exploring the deeper meaning behind life’s challenges and experiences. The session focused on understanding the principles of karma, time, and sanskars, encouraging participants to reflect on their personal journeys and recognize the role of their own actions in shaping outcomes.

The event commenced with a warm welcome by Dr. Manishi, who anchored the session and introduced the guest speaker, BK Sangeeta Didi—a scholar of Vedanta Philosophy and an experienced spiritual guide. She was honored with a plant sapling symbolizing growth and goodwill by Prof. (Dr.) Amita Dev, respected advisor of the Institute. BK Sangeeta Didi led the audience through a calm and reflective discourse, beginning with a guided meditation. She explained the foundational concepts of karma and destiny, emphasizing that every thought and action contributes to one’s karmic account. Through relatable examples and analogies, she illustrated how self-awareness and acceptance can transform one’s perspective and emotional responses.

Key insights included the understanding that: • Every experience is a result of one’s own past actions. • The law of karma governs all aspects of life. • Blame and complaint can be replaced with forgiveness and responsibility. She proposed three transformative affirmations to reset karmic patterns: 1. I am sorry for my past karmic accounts with you. 2. I forgive you for whatever you have done till now. 3. From now onwards, we begin a new karmic account.

The session concluded with a Q&A, where Sangeeta Didi addressed questions on karmic justice and the continuity of the soul’s journey across lifetimes. Her responses reinforced the idea that present circumstances are shaped by past karmas and that spiritual awareness fosters peace and clarity.

A memento was presented to BK Sangeeta Didi by Prof. (Dr.) Amita Dev, followed by closing remarks from Dr. Manishi, who expressed gratitude to all attendees and dignitaries. The session left participants with renewed insight into personal responsibility, forgiveness, and the power of positive thought.
Session on GREEN MAN OF INDIA (22nd April 2024)

The Green Man of India event held on 22nd April, at Main Seminar Hall, aimed to promote environmental awareness and sustainable practices across the country. This Initiative was organized by Value Education Cell on the occasion of “International Earth Day” (A sub event of VASUDHA 2K24). The event featured various activities and one to one conversation with “Vijay Pal Baghel Ji” THE GREEN MAN OF INDIA and discissions centered around the theme of environmental stewardship.

The event started with a warm welcoming speech by VE Cell member ( Malavika Mishra and Aseem Jain). The event commenced with a short skit. (Radha Gupta and Vaishnavi Mishra), which depicted the consequences of environment degradation and the urgent need for collective action to protect our planet. Through the powerful storytelling and compelling performances, the skit conveyed important messages about pollution, deforestation and climate change, urging the audience to reflect on their individual impact on environment. Proceeding further, Our Director General Dr. R.K Agarwal Sir, along with Vijay Pal Baghel ji, graced the occasion. Our Director General Sir, presented Sapling to Mr. Vijay Pal Baghel Ji as a symbolic gesture of environmental preservation. Following this, all attendees gathered to perform Vriksh aarti, a ritualistic worship of trees signifying reverence for nature and its bounty.

After that, Dr. Gopal Babu sir, Co-ordinator VE Cell, delivered a heartfelt speech highlighting Vijay Pal Baghel Ji's contributions to environmental conservation and his role as a champion for sustainability. He emphasized the importance of individuals and institutions coming together to address environmental challenges and create a greener future for generations to come. He also quoted a thought provoking quote from the Upanishad which meant , that if we eat chew nature like honey , then it will also devour us like honey .

Proceeding further, Vijay Pal Baghel ji, in his address, shared insights and inspiration from his journey as an environmentalist. He underscored the urgent need for collective action to protect our planet and preserve its natural resources. He compared pollution with devil which has been ruling all the three realms (Dharti , Aakash, Paataal) from the past 50 years.

Baghel ji also announced the commencement of the global event “Ek Ped Dharti Ke Naam" from our esteemed institution AKGEC Ghaziabad, aimed at promoting tree plantation worldwide. As a symbolic gesture of solidarity and commitment to environmental conservation, Vijay Pal Baghel ji distributed plants to all deans, directors, and the Director General of the college. The dignitaries, along with event attendees (Faculties), proceeded to the mechanical block for a tree plantation drive, symbolizing the collective effort towards a greener future.

Proceeding further, there was a Q/A round, in which all the students participated actively. Proceeding towards the end, a small memento was presented to Mr. Vijay Pal Baghel Ji by Director General Sir.

Lastly, based upon the session, a small quiz and lucky draw was conducted for the students in which they participated actively. The winners were given a chance to interact one to one with Mr. Vijay Pal Baghel Ji The winners were- 1. Himanshi Bharti (CS -1 3rd year) 2. Ayush Maurya (CS-1 3rd year) 3. Aman Rai (CSE-1 2nd year) 4. Mansi Singh (ECE-1st year) 5. Akriti Chug (CSIT-1st year) 6. Ayush Srivastava (CSE AIML-1 2nd year) 7. Manas (ECE-2 2nd year)
Session on International Women’s Day- “Woman- The Foundation of Humanity” (06 March 24) by BK Sangeeta Didi

A profound feeling of festivity for the forthcoming International Women’s Day was exhilaratingly expressed in the event organised by Value Education Cell, AKGEC, Ghaziabad on 6th March 2024. BK Sangeeta Didi, a spiritual Guru and personality of good repute graced the occasion and shared her wisdom on the very apt topic of this special day, “Woman- The Foundation of Humanity”. She generously stated that till the woman takes herself as a gender merely, she feels swings (Depression/Anxiety), unhappiness, complaints and disheartened, but gradually, when she is capable of considering herself as a source of energy, she takes confident steps for the Sanskara (mental impressions) transformation and wisdom development in next generation. She strongly stated that despite all the adversities outside, one may be harmonious in the inner world, and this is true for the constant strength and women's empowerment of changing India and across the globe.

Dr R. K. Agarwal, Director General and Chairperson VE Cell, blessed the ceremony with his visionary words and appreciated women employees’ loyalty, accountability and honesty as strengths of AKGEC. On this occasion, HR Manager Mrs Neelam Chhibber, one of the disciples of Didi, recited a self-written poem, which was appreciated by all attendees. Leadership Qualities for Societal Transformation (01 December 23)

Dates: 01st December, 2023 Duration: 2 Hrs Place: Main Seminar Hall, AKGEC Audience: All HODs, Professors, Associate Professors, FMs and 120 students Topic: Leadership Qualities for Societal Transformation

On December 1st, 2023, VE Cell AKGEC organised a guest lecture titled “Leadership Qualities for Societal Transformation" in the Main Seminar Hall from 10:00 AM to 12:00 PM. The seminar aimed to equip future leaders with the knowledge of societal transformation. To achieve this goal, VE Cell invited Shri Gaurav Bedi, Principal of Gurukul the School and also known as Shri Govind Mohan Das, to deliver a guest lecture on insights derived from the Bhagavad Gita. His lecture aimed to provide practical guidance on cultivating transformative leadership inspired by the timeless wisdom of the Bhagwat Gita.

The session started at 10:00 am with a warm welcoming speech by D.R. Gopal Babu, coordinator, Value Education Cell, preceded by Prof. V.K Parashar, Head, Value Education Cell. Dr. R.K Aggarwal, Director General, AKGEC, presented the token of respect to our guest speaker.

During his lecture, the speaker explained the wisdom of the Bhagwat Gita using characters from the Mahabharata in a natural and understandable way. He was well-versed in understanding the Bhagwat Gita and Ramayana and communicated the concepts in a common language. The participants, All HoDs, Professors, Associate Professors, fifty faculty members and 120 students, were enthusiastic about the content and felt connected with the speaker. Everyone felt that they benefited from the session and desired to invite the speaker again.

In summary, the four pillars are intricately woven together to serve as guiding principles, creating a comprehensive framework that aims to equip participants with a holistic understanding of self and society. By fostering mental wellness and nurturing effective leadership qualities, the seminar aimed to inspire individuals to embark on a transformative journey of personal growth and contribute meaningfully to the betterment of the collective whole.

As the seminar drew to a close, the culmination of insights and shared experiences paved the way for a heartfelt expression of gratitude towards all people involved, directly and indirectly, and our esteemed guest, Shri Govind Mohan Das. In a gesture of appreciation, the Director General presented him with a memento, symbolising the lasting impact of his valuable contributions to the seminar.

Dates: 27th May, 2023 Duration: 1 Hrs Place: CS/IT Seminar Hall, AKGEC Audience: Faculty Members Topic: Dealing with Blame Game

Value Education Cell, AKGEC organized a spiritual seminar on ‘HEALTHY, HAPPY AND HARMONIOUS RELATIONSHIPS’ on 14th October 2022 for all the B.Tech 2nd-year students from 10 AM to 12 PM in the Main Seminar Hall of the administrative block.

The speaker of the session was BK Sangeeta Didi. She, as a spiritualist, has been deeply studying the practical applications of Rajyoga meditation and knowledge in varied fields of life for the last 40 years. She has done spiritual services in many places in India as well as in other countries, including Mauritius, Singapore, Malaysia and Russia. Didi has been a regular facilitator at Air India (for their Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai, Hyderabad and Cochin branches), Jet Airways, Singapore Airlines, Indian Oil Corporation, Ministry of Railways, BHEL, etc.

VE Cell students, Vaishnavi and Aseem, welcomed Didi and briefly introduced the topic to all the dignitaries and audience present in the session. Clarity of relationship and harmony was extracted as everybody’s aspiration, initiating the session. After that, Director General (DG), Dr. RK Agarwal, introduced the esteemed guest BK Sangeeta Didi. He very generously added that he is also under the constant mentoring of Didi. DG’s statement that he is in the “Palna of Didi”, directly touched the audience’s heart and motivated everyone to be more attentive throughout the session.

After DG sir’s address, BK Sangeeta Ji also spoke kind words for such a visionary Director General, who is a guide, a mentor and a well-wisher to his students, rather than only being a Director General of such a prestigious institute. After her one-hour spiritual talk on the topic, she responded to everybody’s questions and doubts with calmness and clarity. She engaged everyone in her speech; the examples she used for better understanding were very much related to day-to-day issues, so they were truly comprehended by everybody. The students and everyone in the hall were impressed and influenced by her simplicity and how she handled the questions. The chanting of OM SHANTI was full of peace and serenity.

She enlightened the minds to understand the real meaning of relationships in life, and she talked about the state of detachment. She perplexed the audience with beautiful lines about relationships like relationships should be based on ‘What we think, feel and interpret’ not on ‘what we speak or how we speak’ No one is wrong, in fact, ‘Each one of us is different’; Don’t just give advice only, ‘Give blessing to the soul to have the power to change the Sanskaar’.

With these blessed lines, she also told about five equations for a harmonious life, listed below: Equation 1: Advise their good, not my mind’s happiness. Equation 2: Everyone is right in their own way Equation 3: Detachment is the best gift for the family because it guarantees that I will be strong and stable whatever happens. Equation 4: I have the potential to respect my pure feelings – whatever happens, being genuine. Equation 5: I will take the initiative to do any pure act.

She helped in observing thoughts, views and issues related to the misconceptions in relationships and gave several examples where life became easy and joyful with the understanding of feelings in a relationship. Various effective examples include mother-children, friends, spouses, etc., and relationships, which almost every one of us often experiences.

Didi also advised everybody to meditate for at least 2-3 minutes between hectic working hours, which certainly boosts productivity, improves mental health, and helps in becoming a better observer of things. She said mediation helps to heal self in difficult situations. She also helped the audience to manage feelings, anger, and emotions while interacting with friends and family.
The session ended with the following homework for the audience to contemplate:

I have great respect for myself – I am a peaceful, loving, happy, very powerful soul, come what may. Even if anyone says something or under any circumstances, no disturbance, dejection,doubt on me the “Soul”or feeling disrespected. I will always create blessings for others.

The powerful session was completed with her blessings. Concluding the event, the honorable DG presented a memento to the charismatic guest as a token of appreciation with a feeling of gratitude. Swati Saxena, VE Cell student, gave a vote of thanks. In the end, a 10-point online Quiz contest based on the contents discussed in the session was conducted, followed by a reward ceremony.
The winners of the quiz were: [1] Vandit Mishra of ECE-3 (Score 10/10) [2] Snehal Shukla of ECE-3 (Score 9/10) [3] Nav Khanna of ECE-2 (Score 9/10)

The feedback from all the participants was very positive and encouraging. Everybody is looking forward to many more such life-related seminars based on spirituality to learn more about self-exploration, self-respect, right understanding, trust and self-evolution.

"Managing Expectations" - A Spiritual talk by Brahma Kumari (BK) Sangeeta Didi (27 November 2021)

Expectations are deeply rooted in every human being. Most of the time, it is the expectations that derives our feelings, thoughts, and actions. However, many times it become a common source of stress in our lives. This happens when expectations exceed the limit. We tend to expect a lot from the person we think close to or loved one. We simply took rights to expect more than our limit toward with whom we are expecting. When the expectation breaks, we tend to lose simple happiness and feel depressed with what we didn’t get. That’s why it becomes important to understand and review our expectations.

In view of the above, VE Cell AKGEC organized an offline session on “Managing Expectations" conducted by BK Sangeeta Didi, a CA and Tax Consultant by profession, now a spiritualist from the well-known organization Brahma Kumaris. She has been a facilitator in many prestigious organizations.

Workshop for female inmates of the Dasna Jail, Ghaziabad

VE Cell AKGEC conducted a 15-day workshop for female inmates of the Dasna Jail, Ghaziabad. We're proud to share the impactful outcomes of the 15-day Universal Human Values workshop held at Dasna Jail! With dedicated sessions spanning two hours each day, female inmates were empowered to embrace important values like trust, respect, affection, and love. Led by the senior UHV Resource Persons, Dr. Parul Verma and Dr. Upasana Mishra, with the help of Dr. Nitya Sharma from AKGEC, Ghaziabad, the workshop fostered empathy and understanding among participants, inspiring them to rise above past mistakes and reshape their futures. By equipping inmates with tools for emotional management and promoting harmonious relationships, this initiative not only enhances the jail atmosphere but also lays a strong foundation for successful societal reintegration post-release. Together, we're building a more compassionate and supportive community.
Significant Outcomes of the Workshop:

• The workshop helped jail inmates understand the importance of human values in their lives and recognise the root cause of problems. • The workshop initiated empathy and respect within inmates, inspiring them to rise above past mistakes and reshape their future. This way, inmates can be guided towards a path of self-improvement, thereby reducing crime propensity and limiting the cycle of imprisonment. • Promoting the release of stress and meaningful relaxation of the mind, inmates learned to manage their emotions more effectively, reducing instances of violence. It helped create a harmonious Jail atmosphere and promoted effective, humane management. • The workshop equipped inmates with the tools and mindset for successful societal reintegration. It empowers them with self-understanding and respect for others, laying the foundation for healthier relationships post-release.
8 Days Teachers’ Orientation Program (TOP) on Vision for Holistic Value-Based Education (22-29 June 2024)

With the vision to spread the ethos of value education, fostering individual and societal transformation through education to achieve a just and equitable society, Value Education Cell AKGEC Ghaziabad conducted an 8-day (22-29 June 2024) Teacher’s Orientation Program for the school teachers of Saraswati Vidya Mandir Rajnagar and Amrapali Global English School, Vasundhara Ghaziabad. As a great success of the previous ‘3-Day TOP’ held during 20 – 22 May 2024 at AKGEC, the 8-Day TOP requested by the principal of Saraswati Vidya Mandir was well accepted by Director General Dr R K Agarwal under the extension activity of VE Cell AKGEC. A total of 41 participants actively attended the TOP. They interacted on various issues and challenges in education in the light of proposals shared with them in a self-explorative manner. The participating teachers strongly felt the need for such holistic education that can help students realise their full human potential to ensure an equitable and just society, as expected in the new National Education Policy.

A few teachers shared their transformative experiences of the program in the presence of the Director General, Dr R K Agarwal, Chairperson, VE Cell AKGEC, along with the chief guests, Ms Deepti Mittal, Director, Saraswati Vidya Mandir Schools, and Mr Pankaj Kumar Sharma principal, Saraswati Vidya Mandir, Rajnagar. These experiences were a testament to the program's positive impact, showing that the participants received the contents well and found them urgently needed by their school teachers and students to move towards a just and equitable society. This success story is a beacon of hope, demonstrating the potential for positive change in our education system.
3 Days Teachers’ Orientation Program (TOP) on Vision for Holistic Value-Based Education (20-22 May 2024)

A 3-day (20-22 May 2024) Teachers’ Orientation Program (TOP) on “The Vision for Holistic Value-Based Education- Realizing the Aspiration articulated in NEP 2020” was organised by Value Education (VE) Cell of Ajay Kumar Garg Engineering College, Ghaziabad. The TOP, a program of utmost importance, was an extension activity of VE Cell as Regional Nodal Centre for Value Education, AKTU, Lucknow. A total of 54 participants, including Principals, Advisors, Academic Coordinators, PGTs, TGTs and Counsellors from 12 schools in Rajasthan, Haryana and Uttar Pradesh, attended the TOP with great enthusiasm and keenness, inspired by the vision of holistic value-based education. The TOP focuses on the role of education in developing human-friendly and nature-friendly mindsets in students through holistic teaching. The sessions include all aspects of human potential, like the mechanism of decision-making, health hygiene, mutually fulfilling interactions, the effort for a just and equitable society, and environmentally responsible conduct, which are aligned with the expectations stated in NEP 2020.

Prof. Gopal Babu, Coordinator, VE Cell was the Resource Person of the TOP. He, with his team members, facilitated and smoothly conducted TOP. The Director, Dr Hemant Ahuja, and Head of VE Cell, Prof V.K. Parashar, inaugurated the session, and the Director General, Dr R.K. Agarwal, graced the closing ceremony of TOP. Shri R.P. Singh, Joint Secretary and Dr Biswajit Saha, Director, Department of Skill Education, CBSE, Ministry of Education, Government of India, New Delhi, were invited as guests in the closing ceremony. The Director General, with both the invited dignitaries, distributed certificates to all the successful participants. The Director General appreciated the team for the successful conduct of the TOP and expressed his generous intent for many more such future programs with the schools that want to be developed as a living model of values. All TOP culminated with a high tea with the participants along the Director General, Deans, HoDs and Section In-charges of the college.
